author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected under the same rules as booking; the correction updates that visit rather than adding another and returns to the owner's record. Reached directly only; no page links to it yet.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction is opened, then the form shows that visit's current date and description
given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit is updated, no visit is added, and the owner's record is shown
given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the visit is unchanged, and the description is named
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the visit is unchanged, and the date is named
edge case 3: opening or submitting a correction for a visit that does not belong to the named pet is refused, and no visit changes
edge case 4: a visit dated today or earlier cannot be saved on its own date; correcting only its description is refused until the date is moved later than today
non_goals: any link or button leading to the correction from the owner's record or elsewhere (owner-deferred to a follow-up request)
new or changed page wording, including the form's heading and submit label, and a confirmation message after a correction
correcting a visit's pet, or any field beyond date and description
notes: Owner-quoted constraints in the intake-decision (line 1) bind the design: the correction's address, reuse of the existing visit form and its model attribute, and validation identical to booking. Narrowest readings taken where the intake was silent, each recorded under PRD Open Questions: no entry link; no wording or confirmation-message change; a past-dated visit cannot keep its date. docs/adr/README.md index needs a row for the 2026-09-29 non-goal ADR; that file is outside this agent's write scope, so system-design-expert or root must add it.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction is the pet-edit pattern applied to visits, inside the owner feature package. Owner stays the aggregate entry point: the handler reaches the visit through Owner.getPet then a new Pet.getVisit lookup, and writes through OwnerRepository by cascade (system-design § Contracts invariants; § Persistence). The one adjustment is VisitController's controller-wide @ModelAttribute("visit") loader. It always creates and attaches a new Visit today, so it must instead resolve the existing visit when a visitId path variable is present, as PetController.findPet does with an optional petId. Validation reuses booking's @NotBlank description and non-future-date rule unchanged; PRD edge case 4 falls out of that rule. No new module, dependency, or ADR. Design writes: requirement id on the Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository and VisitController Contracts rows; one invariant sentence; the visit allow-list in the mass-assignment threat row; a new § Scale and Load section with the visit-lookup row; the ADR index row for the 2026-09-29 non-goal ADR. Resolution basis: grep and file reads (no IDE oracle connected): PetController.java:75 findPet, Owner.java:126 getPet(Integer), VisitController.java:61 loadPetWithVisit.
integration_points: Binding target for GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit: the persisted Visit, model attribute `visit`, behind an allow-list of `date` and `description` (WebDataBinder.setAllowedFields) kept alongside the existing `id`/`*.id` disallow list (security-principles § mass assignment row; system-design § Threat Model mass-assignment row). The allow-list sits on VisitController's binder, so booking gets the same two fields it already posts. The form's hidden petId input is not a Visit property and stays unbound.

Loader: loadPetWithVisit gains an optional visitId path variable (@PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false)). When it is present, it returns pet.getVisit(visitId) and never calls pet.addVisit. If no such visit exists on that pet, it refuses with the same IllegalArgumentException form as the owner and pet refusals beside it (PRD edge case 3). When visitId is absent, booking behaves exactly as today.
Pet.getVisit(Integer id): a domain query mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer). It skips new visits and returns null when none matches.

Success path: owners.save(owner) merges the corrected visit by cascade, then redirects to /owners/{ownerId} with no flash message (a PRD non-goal). Failure path: redisplay pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm and never save; the bound visit is detached because open-in-view is off (system-design § Persistence), so the stored visit stays unchanged.
Template: expected unchanged. The form has no th:action, so it posts to the edit URL; the heading and the 'Add Visit' label stay as they are (PRD non-goal: no wording change).

Test double, OwnerRepository boundary: the existing class-level @MockitoBean stub in VisitControllerTests. Framework stub, reason: OwnerRepository is a JpaRepository whose surface is too wide to hand-write, and a real implementation needs a database-backed context this web-layer test class does not boot (testing-principles § Mocking Policy, tolerated exception). Assert on the owner graph the stub returns: the pet's visit count is unchanged and the corrected visit carries the new fields. Assert that save is called on success and never on refusal.

Test double, framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned web-layer harness (testing-principles § Mocking Policy). Build the fixture's visit behind the test factory (testing-principles, construction behind a factory).

patterns.description: findPet: a controller-wide model-attribute loader with an optional id path variable that returns a new or existing entity
getPet(Integer): identity lookup over an eagerly loaded child collection, skipping unsaved children; the pattern for Pet.getVisit
booking's non-future date rule; correction must share this one check, not copy it

risks.risk: The shared loader keeps attaching a new Visit on the edit route. The save then cascades a blank visit, or the pet gains one in memory, which breaks 'no visit is added' (system-design § Contracts invariants: Visit persisted only by cascade from Owner).
risks.mitigation: The loader branches on visitId as PetController.findPet does; pet.addVisit is reached only when visitId is absent. The in-place test asserts that the pet's visit count is unchanged.

risks.risk: The non-future-date rule is duplicated into a second handler, widening the rules-in-controllers gap (architecture-principles pattern catalog, Web controller row; system-design Open Questions item 2; testing-principles § Test Pyramid).
risks.mitigation: Both handlers call one private check. Moving the rule into the domain stays with the open question and is out of this slice.

risks.risk: The visit lookup scans one pet's visits: the path 'One pet's visits, searched for the visit being corrected' in system-design § Scale and Load.
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: a linear scan over the eagerly loaded set, sized as unrecorded and treated as bounded.

risks.risk: The refusal's exception message reaches the error page, which renders exception messages (system-design § Known Defects; security-principles § secret-disclosure row).
risks.mitigation: The message carries only the owner, pet and visit identifiers from the path, matching the neighboring refusals; it includes no stored field values.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to judge. The product expert wrote the 2026-09-29 non-goal ADR and the 2026-08-08 status line; they are recorded in its prd-entry file_targets and are not claimed here. This dispatch wrote the docs/adr/README.md index row for the new ADR and a status note on the 2026-08-08 row. Open questions, with the narrowest reading taken and no owner answer pending: (1) the Scale and Load figures are unrecorded; (2) 'correction' is not a ubiquitous-language term; the product-requirements-expert may add it, and the code keeps Visit as the noun.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: No test pins the new setAllowedFields allow-list, e.g. a POST to the edit route carrying `firstName` or `id` that asserts the owner and visit id are unchanged. One would keep a future binder edit from silently reopening the Owner rebinding the allow-list now closes.
approved_aspects: Ownership/IDOR: the correction target is re-resolved on every request through the path chain owner -> pet -> visit (VisitController.java loadPetWithVisit: `Visit visit = pet.getVisit(visitId);` then `if (visit == null) { throw new IllegalArgumentException(...)`), so a visitId belonging to another pet or owner is refused on both GET and POST; covered by VisitControllerTests.java:202 `theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedForAVisitNotBelongingToThePet`. Pet.getVisit skips unsaved visits (`!visit.isNew() && Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id)`), so a null id cannot match the transient booking visit.

Mass assignment: the @InitBinder now adds `dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description");` beside the existing `setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")`. Because the binder is unnamed it also applies to the `@ModelAttribute Owner owner` handler parameter, which previously could be rebound (firstName, address, ...) through the visit POST routes. That is a strict tightening over the baseline, not a regression; the only field sweep hit in the diff is this controller (`@ModelAttribute` grep over the changed production files).

Validation on the save path: processUpdateVisitForm takes `@Valid Visit visit` (Visit.description is `@NotBlank`) and applies the same future-date rule as booking through the shared `rejectDateNotInFuture`. Saving happens only when BindingResult has no errors, and `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false` (application.properties:11) means the detached entity mutated by a rejected bind is never flushed.

Error disclosure: the new IllegalArgumentException message carries only the integer path ids (ownerId, petId, visitId typed int/Integer, so no request text), matching the existing owner/pet messages in the same method. error.html:18 renders it with escaped `th:text="${message}"`.

XSS/template: no template changed in this diff. The visit form renders description via escaped `th:text`, and the `__${name}__` preprocessing in fragments/inputField.html takes fixed literals ('date', 'description'), never request text.

Exposed surface: the two new routes, GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, are open like every other route under the demonstration baseline in docs/security-principles.md. They mutate only date/description of an existing visit, and no management exposure changes.
Secrets: grep of the added diff lines for password|secret|token|apikey|api_key|credential|jdbc: returned no hits.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set and no dependency changed. No OWASP Dependency-Check plugin is configured (grep -F -i 'dependencycheck' build.gradle had no hits), so no NVD match ran in this review. Resolved versions from `./gradlew dependencies`: Spring Boot 4.1.1 starters, jackson-databind (tools.jackson) 3.1.5, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, Hibernate 7.4.5.Final.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The slice edits the visit binder (VisitController.setAllowedFields now allows only date and description; id and *.id stay disallowed) and system-design.md's threat model row on identifier tampering names it as the mitigation for the new edit route. No test submits an id field to the correction route. Removing the id disallow or the allowlist would let a form rewrite the identity of the visit being corrected, and the suite would stay green. Checked with grep -F for '"id"', 'param("id' and 'setAllowedFields' across src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/*.java: no match. A valid-correction POST that also carries an id param (a different value from BOOKED_VISIT_ID) would fail on that change.
findings.fix: Add a test, or extend theVisitCorrectionShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlaceAndShowTheOwner, that POSTs the correction with an extra id param set to a value other than BOOKED_VISIT_ID and asserts, with the existing recursive comparison, that the visit keeps BOOKED_VISIT_ID. Name the id value as a Tier 1 constant.

Mockito use stays within the brief's tolerated stubs: the repository stub is pre-existing, and the save verifications assert the write, which is the contract (Owner is the sole write path per system-design.md).

author: change-grader
summary: add in-place correction of a booked visit's date and description

blast_radius.note: Two production files in one package (Pet gains a lookup, VisitController gains an optional visitId and two edit handlers), 67 prod lines, no sensitive paths; the docs edits are the PRD row, one new non-goal ADR, and design-doc coherence lines.

semantic_surprise.note: The one line that reaches past the new routes is the controller-wide setAllowedFields("date", "description"): it also narrows binding on the existing booking POST and on the @ModelAttribute Owner, closing an Owner rebinding path. The design block recorded this as intended, and no legitimate form field is lost. The edit path mutates a detached visit, and it never flushes on refusal because open-in-view=false (application.properties:11). The form has no action, so it posts back to the edit URL.

test_adequacy.note: The correction tests are real: recursive whole-visit comparisons, never-save on refusal, a foreign-visit refusal on GET and POST, and an isNew guard test in PetTests. But the new allow-list itself is unpinned. The TAMPERED_VISIT_ID test posts id, which setDisallowedFields already blocked, so it stays green if setAllowedFields is deleted. No test posts an Owner field such as firstName to either visit route.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved, but the security reviewer's recommendation that no test pins the allow-list against Owner rebinding went unaddressed. The test reviewer's round-2 claim that the id test "would fail if the id disallow or the allowlist were removed" does not hold for the allow-list alone. The security reviewer's absence from the round-2 fix-delta roster is expected.

scope_deviation.note: Routes, validation, the in-place update, and the redirect match the intake bullets; no link is added, and NG-5 is narrowed through its own ADR as the owner directed. The booking-route binder change came from the triage design block, not from a fix round. The fix round changed only one docs line and one test, with zero retries, consultations, or design revisions.

rationale: The feature is contained and matches its brief. The residual risk is a new controller-wide binder allow-list that also tightens the booking route and closes Owner rebinding, but no test pins it and a reviewer overstated that one does. Read VisitController.setAllowedFields and the TAMPERED_VISIT_ID test before merging, and consider adding a firstName-rebinding test.
